questions.q: According to the Meghalaya Government release dated 28 October 2026, the Golden Jubilee presentation for Wangala plans to feature how many drums?
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — 1,000.
Key points: The State Government's 28 October release says the 50th organised celebration of the 100 Drums Wangala Festival will feature a special presentation with 1,000 drums. It identifies Wangala as a Garo post-harvest thanksgiving festival associated with Misi Saljong.
Why the other options are incorrect: 100 is the traditional festival name; 500 and 1,500 are not the number stated in the release.
Exam takeaway: Keep the one-off Golden Jubilee arrangement separate from the festival's traditional name.
Source: Meghalaya Government press release, 28-10-2026 — https://www.meghalaya.gov.in/press/content/52221

questions.q: For how long will Meghalaya's Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 remain in force from the date of notification in the Official Gazette?
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — Three years.
Key points: The Meghalaya Government's 22 October 2026 release says the EV Policy 2026 will remain in force for three years from the date of notification in the Official Gazette. It supersedes the Meghalaya Electric Vehicle Policy, 2021.
Why the other options are incorrect: One, two and five years do not match the duration specified in the official release.
Exam takeaway: For policy questions, distinguish the announcement date from the policy's legal commencement date: the duration runs from Gazette notification.
Source: Meghalaya Government press release, 22-10-2026 — https://www.meghalaya.gov.in/press/content/52135

questions.q: Reuters reported that the Indian rupee gained approximately how much month-on-month in October 2026, its strongest monthly performance since February?
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — About 1%.
Key points: Reuters reported on 30 October 2026 that the rupee had gained about 1% during October and closed at ₹94.95 per US dollar. The report linked the improvement partly to RBI measures to curb dollar demand and support the currency.
Why the other options are incorrect: 0.25%, 0.5% and 2% do not match the approximate monthly gain reported.
Exam takeaway: Exchange-rate figures are time-specific. Memorise the reporting date and do not treat a market close as a permanent rate.
Source: Reuters, 30-10-2026 — https://www.reuters.com/world/india/rupee-benefit-dollar-retreat-plunging-us-yields-oil-surge-tempers-impact-2026-10-30/

questions.q: A high-level committee constituted by India's Finance Ministry on 30 October 2026 was reported to review which sector?
questions.e:
Correct answer: A — Banking sector.
Key points: Reuters reported on 30 October 2026 that the Finance Ministry had established a high-level committee to review India's banking sector and identify reforms that could help banks support economic growth and improve global competitiveness.
Why the other options are incorrect: The report specifically identifies banking; it does not describe a committee for telecom, agricultural marketing or civil aviation.
Exam takeaway: The reported purpose was to review and recommend banking reforms. The report did not specify membership, detailed terms of reference or a completion date.
Source: Reuters, 30-10-2026 — https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-constitutes-high-level-committee-banking-reforms-2026-10-30/

questions.q: According to Reuters on 29 October 2026, the Green Climate Fund approved US$1.97 billion for how many projects at its latest board meeting?
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — 21 projects.
Key points: Reuters reported that the Green Climate Fund approved US$1.97 billion across 21 projects. The approvals brought the fund's total 2026 funding to a reported record US$3.2 billion.
Why the other options are incorrect: The report gives 21 as the number of approved projects; 12, 18 and 30 are not the reported count.
Exam takeaway: The Green Climate Fund is a multilateral climate-finance mechanism that supports developing countries' climate action.
Source: Reuters, 29-10-2026 — https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/cop/green-climate-fund-approves-record-near-2-billion-funding-2026-10-29/

questions.q: Pipe A can fill an empty tank in 8 hours, while Pipe B can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If both pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — 24 hours.
Key points: Work rates are measured as fractions of one tank per hour. Pipe A fills 1/8 tank per hour; Pipe B empties 1/12 tank per hour, so its rate is negative.
Step-by-step calculation:
1. Net rate = 1/8 − 1/12.
2. LCM of 8 and 12 is 24: 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24 tank per hour.
3. Time = 1 tank ÷ (1/24 tank per hour) = 24 hours.
Why the other options are incorrect: They do not equal the reciprocal of the net filling rate. Adding the two rates would be wrong because one pipe empties the tank.
Exam takeaway: For an inlet and outlet working together, add filling rates and subtract emptying rates. Keep the unit as tank/hour until the final time is calculated.
Source: Original aptitude practice; independently checked using the standard work-rate method — https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.q: A trader mixes 20 kg of rice costing ₹40 per kg with 30 kg costing ₹50 per kg. What is the average cost per kilogram of the mixture?
questions.e:
Correct answer: C — ₹46 per kg.
Key points: The average cost is a weighted average because the two quantities are different. Multiply each quantity by its unit price, add the costs, and divide by the total quantity.
Step-by-step calculation:
1. Cost of first lot = 20 kg × ₹40/kg = ₹800.
2. Cost of second lot = 30 kg × ₹50/kg = ₹1,500.
3. Total cost = ₹800 + ₹1,500 = ₹2,300; total quantity = 20 + 30 = 50 kg.
4. Average cost = ₹2,300 ÷ 50 kg = ₹46 per kg.
Why the other options are incorrect: ₹44, ₹45 and ₹48 do not equal the total weighted cost divided by the total 50 kg.
Exam takeaway: Do not take the simple average of ₹40 and ₹50 unless both quantities are equal. Use total cost ÷ total quantity.
Source: Original quantitative-aptitude practice; calculation independently checked — https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.q: Neither the clerk nor the officers ___ present during the inspection.
questions.e:
Correct answer: B — were.
Key points: In the correlative construction “neither … nor”, the verb commonly agrees with the nearer subject. Here the nearer subject is “the officers”, which is plural, so the plural verb “were” is used.
Why the other options are incorrect: “Was” and “is” are singular; “has been” is also singular and does not agree with the nearer plural subject.
Exam takeaway: With either/or and neither/nor, check the subject nearest to the verb. Avoid letting the first noun control the verb automatically.
Source: Original grammar practice; see the British Council grammar reference — https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/english-grammar-reference
